metadata.title: Gaia TGAS search for Large Magellanic Cloud runaway supergiant stars:Candidate hypervelocity star discovery, and the nature of R71

evidence.quote: Sk-67 2 (HIP 22237), is a candidate hypervelocity star, the TGAS proper motion implying a very large peculiar transverse velocity (∼360 km/s) directed radially away from the LMC centre.

Sk-67 2 (HIP 22237), is a candidate hypervelocity star, the TGAS proper motion implying a very large peculiar transverse velocity (∼360 km/s) directed radially away from the LMC centre.
Therefore Sk-67 2 is clearly unbound with respect to the LMC and, as we argue below, a possible hypervelocity star.
We conclude that Sk-67 2 is a candidate hypervelocity star that if confirmed, by for example Gaia Data Release 2 (DR2), would warrant further investigation as to the nature of its origin.

values.condition: Measured from weak metal lines in high-resolution FEROS 2004 and VLT/UVES 2001 and 2012 spectra; the same value was obtained for all three epochs.

notes: Sk-67 2: The paper explicitly calls it a candidate hypervelocity star and states that it is clearly unbound with respect to the LMC (T:p4-b8; T:p5-b7), but does not explicitly establish present-day unboundness from the Milky Way; the inclusion reflects the paper’s retained hypervelocity/unbound-from-LMC candidacy. The correspondence Sk-67 2 = HDE 270754 = HIP 22237, its alias R 51, and its Gaia DR1 source ID are supported by I:p4-b4 and I:p7-b0.

Sk-67 2: The table reports peculiar velocity components v_W = 251.4 ± 27.8 km/s and v_N = 256.7 ± 24.6 km/s relative to the van der Marel & Sahlmann model, and a peculiar transverse speed v_t = 359.3 ± 26.2 km/s (T:p7-b0); these are not equatorial proper-motion components or a Galactic-rest-frame total speed. The paper states Sk-67 2 is clearly unbound with respect to the LMC (T:p4-b8), but gives no bound/unbound probability. Its quoted distance of about 3.5 kpc is from the LMC centre (T:p5-b2, T:p5-b4), not the Galactic centre. No right ascension, declination, parallax, or equatorial proper-motion values are reported. The 50.1 ± 2.5 kpc value is an adopted LMC distance for velocity conversion (T:p2-b7), while 50.6 kpc is a conditional distance from the position/velocity geometry (T:p5-b2).
